# `cis_extensions.dns_logging` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/cis-extensions/dns-logging.satz`

## Purpose

CIS 5.0 §2.13 — DNS query logging, as far as an org policy can carry it.

WHAT THE CONTROL ASKS. Every VPC network has a Cloud DNS policy with logging enabled,
so name resolution is auditable — which is how a compromised host asking for its
command-and-control domain becomes visible. New in CIS 5.0; the 4.0 catalog has no
such control.

WHAT A CONSTRAINT CAN AND CANNOT DO, stated plainly because the difference decides
the claim. An org-policy constraint judges a resource being CREATED or UPDATED. It
can therefore refuse a DNS policy that has logging off, which is what this pack
enforces. It cannot require that a resource EXIST: nothing in an org policy can say
"every network must have a DNS policy attached", because the network is not the
resource being changed and carries no reference to one. So this is a `contributes`
claim, not an `implements` — no org policy discharges §2.13 on its own, and the
missing half is a network that simply has no policy at all.

THE MISSING HALF IS THE ESTATE'S. A network the estate declares gets its policy from
the estate (`google_dns_policy` with `enable_logging = true`, naming that network);
a network a customer's workload team made in their own project is where
`report-compliance` earns its keep — it reads the live state and names the networks
without logging. That list is the worklist; this constraint is what keeps it from
growing.

WHAT IT COSTS. DNS query logs are charged as logging volume and are small beside flow
logs — one entry per query, no payload. There is no sampling knob: logging is on or
off per policy.

ON BY DEFAULT, like flow logs, and for the same reason: a customer switching it off
is deciding not to see name resolution, and that decision belongs in a `deviates`
claim whose `reason` the compliance report carries.

## Use it

```
params {
  cis_dns_logging = true
}

use "presets/cis-extensions/dns-logging.satz" when cis_dns_logging
```

`cis_dns_logging` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `CIS_GCP_Foundation_4_0`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

_None — the pack takes everything from the estate's params._

## Claims

| framework | control | title | kind | witnesses | interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cis-gcp 5.0 | 2.13 | Cloud DNS logging on all VPC networks | contributes | `google_org_policy_custom_constraint.cis_dns_logging`<br>`google_org_policy_policy.custom_cisDnsPolicyLogging` | A Cloud DNS policy cannot be created or updated with query logging off. |

**What the controls ask** (this project's paraphrase from the catalog — never the framework's own text):

- **Cloud DNS logging on all VPC networks** (cis-gcp 5.0 §2.13) — Every VPC network has a DNS policy with logging enabled so name resolution is auditable.

**Manual duties** (a control stays *partial* until each is attested):

- `attach-policy` (cis-gcp 5.0 §2.13) — The control also asks that every VPC network HAS such a policy, which no org policy can require: the estate declares one per network it owns, and report-compliance names the networks that have none.

Every resource this pack contributes is a witness of a claim above.
